title: Cantilever column with axial load and a small lateral load: second-order moment and deflection - values printed by the vendor that do not reproduce

source.work: Bentley Systems, STAAD.Pro Help, Verification Examples (public documentation, docs.bentley.com)
source.edition: STAAD.Pro Help v21 build (pages refer to the STAAD.Pro 2023 sample files), read 2026-11-22
source.notes: problem statement taken from the vendor page (text and input listing). The page cites: AISC, Specification for Structural Steel Buildings, 2005, p. 16.1-435, Case 2 (the 2005 edition was not opened; the same benchmark of the 2022 edition is in ../aisc-commentary) - NOT opened for this project; no number is taken from it. The page's 'theory' values are recorded as printed; the program's own results are not used.

analysis: Plane problem in the global X-Y plane (Y vertical); the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held; in-plane bending about local z. Cantilever column of 300 in, built in at the base, free at the top; W8x18 with the moment of inertia the page gives, Iz = 61.9 in^4, E = 29,000 ksi; axial load 30 kip and lateral load 0.09 kip at the top. Combination 'second': second-order analysis of both loads (the engine's member carries the exact stability functions); combination 'first': first-order analysis of the lateral load alone. The area does not enter the targets (placeholder 10 in^2); Iy = 1000 Iz so that no out-of-plane buckling enters. The lateral load is 0.003 x 30 kip = 0.09 kip (the page's text has '0.03 x 30'; its arithmetic uses 0.09). The page's closed form uses the full E (no stiffness reduction).  Same model as problem 'cantilever-column-notional-load' (whose recomputed targets are active); the targets here are the vendor's printed values only.

targets.precisionNote: printed "61.37"; tolerance = half a unit in the last printed digit; the page's reference maximum moment
targets.sign: the page prints a magnitude; sign from the reference solution, engine convention (docs/CONVENTIONS.md)

targets.precisionNote: printed "1.145"; tolerance = half a unit in the last printed digit; the page's reference maximum deflection

quarantine.diagnosis: Both values missed by 2.0 times the tolerance: moment engine 61.380 kip in, printed 61.37; deflection engine 1.1460 in, printed 1.145. Cause: rounding in the page's hand evaluation of the closed form. The page carries alpha = 1.226, tan(alpha)/alpha = 2.273 and M0 = 2.25 ft kip and prints '5.115 ft k = 61.37 in k' although 5.115 x 12 = 61.38; for the deflection it multiplies 0.451 by 2.537. In double precision the same closed forms give alpha = 1.22642, M = 0.09 x 300 x 2.273332 = 61.380 kip in and delta = 0.451228 x 2.539731 = 1.14600 in, the ODE oracle's and the engine's values. The program results printed on the same page are 61.36 and 1.14538.
